title: Avalon Pilot - Week 3 Security & Results Standup
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-08-05 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Location: Zoom | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Avalon); Liam O'Connor (Avalon Sec); Sandra Kim (Avalon PM); Ethan Park (Avalon QA)
summary: Week 3 pilot checkpoint: reviewed end-to-end results from the sandbox workloads, discussed SSO/SAML integration status, audit logs format and retention policy, SOC 2 evidence requests and how Redwood can provide artifacts. SE walked through latency/cost tradeoffs observed in the pilot and suggested tuning + dedicated KV cache settings. Action items focused on sharing SOC2 docs, updating SSO metadata, and running a short 5k-conversation replay for audit log verification.
topics: Pilot results overview and perf numbers
action_items: Diego Ruiz - Package and share SOC2 evidence checklist & redacted report link by 2025-08-07
Maya Chen - Send updated SSO metadata example and entityID to Liam, include ACS URL; due 2025-08-06
Priya Nair - Confirm list of auditors who will need access; due 2025-08-08
Ethan Park - Kick off 5k convo replay on staging and report mismatches by 2025-08-11
Sandra Kim - Share privacy/data retention policy requirements doc; due 2025-08-07
next_steps: Redwood to deliver SOC2 artifact bundle + secure link
Avalon to update IdP with Redwood SAML metadata and test SSO on staging
Run audit-log replay and validate field mappings
Schedule on-site security review if auditors request deeper evidence (tentative week of 2025-08-18)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick 45 minute standup — primarily security items and the week 3 pilot results. Diego will run the perf stuff. Priya, Liam, Sandra, Ethan, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Priya: Yep, thanks Maya. We got a couple folks pulled in, Liam had an urgent ticket but joined.
[00:22] Liam: Hi all, I'm on. Quick note, I'm mostly focused on the SSO and audit log mapping.
[00:30] Diego: Cool. I'll start with a short run-down of the sandbox telemetry we collected overnight. These are synthetic shopping queries — about 2.1k total requests, bursty during catalog updates.
[00:42] Diego: P50 latency ~85 ms, P95 ~220 ms on the hosted small endpoint. Cost estimate per 1k tokens about $0.55 in this config. We saw KV-cache hit rate at about 18% — that's low because of the test harness randomness.
[00:58] Ethan: When you say KV-cache hit, is that per customer or per model? I'm not sure how to map to our QA scripts.
[01:06] Diego: It's per model instance, so when we pin model v1.2 you'll see it stabilize. For the pilot, we suggested toggling conservative caching to bump hit rate — that'll give you lower token spend but a small cold-start risk.
[01:22] Maya: Quick question for Avalon — what's the acceptable retention for request/response pairs in audit logs for compliance?
[01:29] Sandra: We need 12 months for incident forensics, but PII must be redacted or tokenized. We also have an internal policy for deletion after 18 months unless legal hold.
[01:42] Liam: Right. On top of that, auditors will want to see immutable audit logs and proof of tamper-resistance. Can you outline how Redwood's audit logs look today?
[01:50] Diego: Sure. Current hosted audit logs include timestamp, request_id, model_name, route, token_count, request_headers (with masked Authorization), a hash of the output (we can include a salted checksum), and a pointer to encrypted blob storage for the full transcript when enabled. We don't store raw creds.
[02:10] Priya: Is the blob storage access restricted via KMS? That's non-negotiable for us.
[02:16] Diego: Yes, all persistent storage is customer-segregated and supports KMS-based envelope encryption. We can provide an architecture diagram and the KMS integration steps.
[02:25] Liam: Who manages the keys in the hosted offering? Avalon wants BYOK if possible.
[02:30] Maya: We support both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK via your cloud KMS; for Dedicated/Private we recommend customer-managed keys. We'll note that in the artifacts.
[02:38] Sandra: On SSO — we tried the metadata you sent but got a mismatch on the ACS URL during the first test.
[02:45] Diego: Ah, that's likely the entityID/ACS mismatch — did you use the staging-redirect endpoint? There are two ACS endpoints depending on the routing. I'll paste an updated metadata snippet after the call.
[02:56] Liam: Also need to confirm NameID format — some of our IdP rules require persistent NameIDs, and our SCIM mapping expects email as primary.
[03:05] Maya: Good call. Diego, can you confirm NameID support?
[03:09] Diego: We support transient and persistent NameID. SCIM user provisioning is available on Dedicated and Private today; for hosted we can enable SCIM on a case-by-case basis but you'll want to use JIT provisioning for the pilot.
[03:22] Priya: We will likely need SCIM for the auditors to show user lifecycle. If hosted can't do full SCIM, what about a short-term workaround?
[03:31] Diego: We can provide a user sync tool — basically a one-time sync to seed users and group membership, and then continue with JIT for subsequent changes. It's not ideal long-term but works for pilot.
[03:40] Ethan: For the audit replays — how granular are the logs? We need request/response pairs and a mapping back to session IDs for our test harness.
[03:48] Diego: The logs include session_id, request_id, and a stable conversation_id. We can export to JSONL with a schema that matches your replay harness.
[03:57] Sandra: Can you show an example quickly?
[04:00] Diego: Yeah, here's an example in the doc linked in the deck — I'll paste link in chat: https://redwood.com/security/audit-log-sample (note: placeholder). The fields might be slightly different in the hosted prod build versus the staging shim.
[04:14] Liam: Regarding tamper-resistance, we need attestations for write-once storage or append-only logs. Is your blob store append-only or can objects be deleted?
[04:23] Diego: The object store supports object immutability flags and WORM configurations for enterprise customers; we can enable an append-only policy for your retention window. For hosted customers we have a contractual addendum for that.
[04:35] Priya: Good. On SOC 2 — our audit team asked for evidence of change management and incident postmortems for the last six months. Can you provide a redacted bundle?
[04:46] Maya: Yes, we can provide a redacted SOC 2 package and an evidence checklist. Diego will prepare that. We'll redact customer names and sensitive IP.
[04:55] Diego: I'll put together the package and a short README that maps each auditor question to a doc. Expect a secure link.
[05:02] Priya: Timeline?
[05:05] Diego: I can deliver by tomorrow EOD — aiming 2025-08-07 in your timezone.
[05:10] Sandra: We also had a question about data residency — some of our EU customers require logs to be stored in region. Can Redwood route logs to an EU bucket?
[05:19] Diego: Yes, with Private or Dedicated you can pin region for storage; for hosted we can configure regional buckets during onboarding — depends on availability and compliance plan. We'll confirm latency impacts.
[05:29] Maya: Switching back to perf briefly — Diego you mentioned cost tradeoffs. Can you suggest a config for more stable P95 and lower cost?
[05:36] Diego: For your workload, enabling prefix caching for catalog queries and bumping batch-size to 8 in off-peak windows will drop P95 by ~30% and reduce token cost by ~12%. We can also recommend model quantization to int8 if quality tests pass — that'll cut GPU memory and cost but requires evaluation.
[05:54] Ethan: Quantization worries me — we've seen degraded answers in other vendors. How will you guard against quality regression?
[06:01] Diego: We run evals tied to your prompt set and have regression alerts; we can run a canary quantized model against the baseline and produce diffs for the top 20 intents. If you see drift we'll roll back.
[06:13] Priya: For our pilot acceptance criteria — we need P95 below 350 ms for search flows, costs under $0.75 per 1k tokens for standard prompts, and SOC2 evidence. Are we aligned?
[06:25] Maya: Sounds reasonable. Diego, can you map current numbers to those thresholds?
[06:29] Diego: Current P95 is 220 ms, so we're within the latency goal. Cost is lower already at $0.55 per 1k tokens in this config. The outstanding item is SOC2 docs and SSO confirmation.
[06:40] Liam: On the SSO test we ran, the SAML response had an unexpected audience value — maybe the metadata still had the production audience. We'll need a metadata refresh.
[06:50] Diego: Noted. Maya, I'll send a metadata v2 and a quick checklist for IdP config items.
[06:56] Maya: Great. A couple more items — audit export format: do you support streaming to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/Elastic)?
[07:04] Diego: We support pushing to Pub/Sub/Kinesis and S3 exports; for SIEMs we can integrate via webhook or a forwarder. The fastest path is S3 -> Lambda -> ingestion, but we can do direct streams too.
[07:18] Sandra: For the audit exports, we need field-level encryption for PII. Can you encrypt the user_email field separately?
[07:26] Diego: We can redaction-mask or field-encrypt specific columns using envelope encryption with your KMS. It's an enterprise feature but doable for the pilot as a temporary config.
[07:37] Priya: Okay — that's promising. Now, on evidence handoff: auditors often ask for live access to logs for short windows. How does Redwood provide that without exposing other tenants?
[07:47] Diego: We'll give scoped, time-limited access to your own logging namespace, using a signed URL and role-based credentials. All accesses are audited and we can produce an access report.
[07:56] Liam: Please include IP allowlisting for auditor sessions.
[07:59] Diego: We'll note that.
[08:02] Maya: Quick status check — who's owning the SSO test case?
[08:06] Liam: I'll own the test and coordinate with Diego on metadata.
[08:09] Sandra: I'll own the retention mapping and legal hold requirements.
[08:13] Ethan: I'll start the 5k conversation replay on staging and report back.
[08:17] Diego: One more perf note — we recommend setting the autoscale buffer to 15% for predictable latency during catalog refresh spikes; that avoids cold-start amplification.
[08:28] Priya: Is that available in hosted?
[08:31] Diego: Yes, the buffer is configurable. For Dedicated you get more control over the pool size.
[08:37] Maya: Any blockers on Redwood side to providing the SOC2 artifacts and updated SAML metadata?
[08:42] Diego: No blockers. I'll upload the SOC2 bundle to a secure share and send SAML metadata in the next 24 hours.
[08:49] Maya: Great. Any open questions from the Avalon side that we haven't covered?
[08:54] Priya: Two micro items: auditor access window length — they want 48 hrs; is that doable? And logging retention must be immutable for 12 months.
[09:04] Diego: 48 hr signed access is fine; we can enable immutability for 12 months via WORM policy.
[09:11] Priya: Perfect.
[09:13] Sandra: Also, can you provide a mapping doc that ties Redwood controls to SOC2 criteria (CC7, etc.)? That's what the auditors request.
[09:21] Maya: Yes, Diego, can you include that in the evidence package?
[09:24] Diego: On it. I'll map controls to trust services criteria and include references to the relevant runbooks.
[09:30] Ethan: Last thing — for the replay mismatches, what's the expected turnaround?
[09:35] Diego: If you run the replay and flag mismatches, we aim for a 3-business-day triage by SEs to root cause (config vs model drift).
[09:44] Priya: OK. That seems reasonable.
[09:47] Maya: Quick recap — Diego will share SOC2 artifacts and controls mapping by 2025-08-07; Diego will share SAML metadata v2 by 2025-08-06; Avalon will run 5k replay and report by 2025-08-11; we'll tentatively schedule an on-site security review the week of 2025-08-18 if auditors request.
[10:10] Liam: Sounds good.
[10:12] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send meeting notes and a short checklist.
[10:17] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:20] [call ends]

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-hearings and shorthand; links referenced in chat are placeholders and will be replaced by secure shares in Redwood follow-up.
